name: Find Google Maps companies with BasedOnBusiness and add them to HubSpot without duplicates

parameters.content:
## Turn a Google Maps search into clean HubSpot companies

### Who is it for

B2B sales teams and lead generation agencies who work out of HubSpot and want local company records they can call, without hand-copying them from Google Maps.

### How it works

Fill in the form: business category, city, country and how many leads to collect. **BasedOnBusiness** searches current Google Maps business data. The workflow keeps only businesses that have a website and enough reviews to look established, reduces each website to a bare domain, and then walks the list one company at a time.

For every company it asks HubSpot whether that domain already exists. Known companies are skipped; only new ones are created. That is the point of the template — **run the same search next month and your CRM does not fill up with duplicates.**

Each new HubSpot company record gets the business name, domain, website, phone, street address, city, country, and a short description carrying the Google Maps category, rating and review count.

### Requirements

- A **BasedOnBusiness** account and API key — https://www.basedonb.com/
- A **HubSpot** account. The free CRM is enough.
- API reference and setup guide — https://www.basedonb.com/en/docs

### How to set up

**1.** Open **Start BasedOnBusiness Search** and add an *HTTP Bearer Auth* credential holding your API key, with the `scrapes:read` and `scrapes:write` scopes. The other two BasedOnBusiness nodes reuse it.

**2.** In HubSpot, go to *Settings → Integrations → Service Keys* and create a service key with the `crm.objects.companies.read` and `crm.objects.companies.write` scopes. In n8n, create a **HubSpot App Token** credential and paste the service key into it. Both HubSpot nodes use that one credential.

**3.** Click **Test workflow** and run a small search first.

### How to customize

- Raise **Minimum reviews** to keep only established businesses, or drop it to 0 to take everything with a website.
- Change **Skip Existing** to a HubSpot *Company → Update* node if you would rather refresh known records than leave them alone.
- Add fields to **Create Company in HubSpot** from the Google Maps data, for example the rating as a custom property.

### Good to know

A search costs BasedOnBusiness credits equal to the **Number of leads** you request, not the number of companies that survive the filter or get created in HubSpot.

Businesses with no website are dropped here on purpose: the domain is what HubSpot deduplicates on. If you want the no-website ones instead, they are a separate prospect list.

## Step 1 — Describe the companies you want

Category, city and a two-letter country code, plus the fewest reviews a business needs before it counts as established.

**Prepare Search** rejects bad input before any credits are spent.

## Step 2 — Start the search

Creates the BasedOnBusiness job.

`Idempotency-Key` stops a retry from being billed twice.

## Step 3 — Wait for the search to finish

BasedOnBusiness collects the data in the background, so the workflow polls the job every **15 seconds** until its status is `done`.

The loop stops on a `failed` or `cancelled` job, and gives up after **15 minutes**, so it can never run forever.

## Step 4 — Keep the companies worth adding

The finished job is split into one item per business. **Qualified Companies** keeps those that have a website and at least your minimum review count, and drops anything permanently closed.

## Step 5 — Reduce each website to a domain

HubSpot deduplicates companies on the domain, so `https://www.example.com/contact` and `example.com` have to collapse to the same key before anything is looked up.

The list is then walked one company at a time.

## Step 6 — Ask HubSpot first, then create

For each company the workflow searches HubSpot for that domain.

- **Found** — the company is already in your CRM, so it is skipped and nothing is overwritten.
- **Not found** — a new company record is created.

This is what keeps a repeated search from filling HubSpot with duplicates.
